name: imessage-mcp
description: Search and read your Apple Messages history. Read-only, runs on your Mac.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Search messages by substring, exact text, token, or phrase.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Read a conversation with edits, reactions, receipts, replies, and attachments.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: Find conversations by contact, service, kind, reply state, or date.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Show one attachment: images with metadata removed, text files as text.

tools.name: sync_messages
tools.description: Pull new, edited, unsent, and deleted messages, reactions, and receipts since a cursor.

tools.name: analyze_communication
tools.description: Message counts, activity, response times, and initiation.

tools.name: resolve_contact
tools.description: Match a name or handle to a contact without guessing.

tools.name: server_status
tools.description: Version, update availability, index state, and Contacts access.

prompts.name: catch_up
prompts.description: Who is waiting on you across your recent conversations, and what they need.
prompts.text: This iMessage server is read-only: it cannot send, react, or mark anything read. Catch me up on my messages from the last three days. Call list_conversations once; each conversation includes its latest_message. Anyone whose latest message is incoming and needs a reply is waiting on me; skip verification codes and automated senders. Read a thread with get_conversation only when the latest message does not say what they need. Tell me, most urgent first, who is waiting on me and what they need, one short line each. If nothing is waiting, say so plainly.

prompts.name: draft_reply
prompts.description: A reply in your own texting style to whoever is waiting on you. It is never sent.
prompts.text: This iMessage server is read-only: it cannot send, react, or mark anything read. Draft a reply for me to the most recent conversation from the last three days whose latest_message is incoming, or to the person I name, found with resolve_contact. Read it with get_conversation and match my own texting style in that thread. Return one draft only, and remind me in one short line that I have to send it myself.

prompts.name: recap
prompts.description: This week in messages: volume, busiest conversations, and anyone still waiting.
prompts.text: This iMessage server is read-only: it cannot send, react, or mark anything read. Recap my last seven days of messages. Use analyze_communication with metric message_count, which includes by_hour and by_weekday, and list_conversations with order most_messages: how many I sent and received, when I was most active, my busiest conversations, and anyone whose latest message still needs a reply. Keep it to a few short lines and do not quote message text.

privacy.title: Privacy mode
privacy.description: full, redacted, or aggregate. redacted shows names and masked handles with no message text; aggregate shows counts only.

contacts.title: Contact names
contacts.description: live reads your unified Contacts to name handles. none leaves handles unnamed.

update_check.title: Check for updates
update_check.description: When on, server status makes one anonymous request to the public npm registry to see whether a newer version exists. No message or contact data is sent.

long_description: Lets Claude search and read the iMessage, SMS, MMS, and RCS history already stored in Messages on your Mac: find messages, read conversations with edits and reactions, see photos with location data removed, follow new messages, and answer counts and response-time questions. It cannot send, edit, or delete messages. Everything runs locally; there are no accounts or telemetry. Claude needs Full Disk Access to read Messages.
